areas.title: Abstract Management (Review Depth & Disposition)

items.reasoning: The Evaluation Plan page is explicitly round-based ('Add round', 'Edit dates, blind review, reviewer pools, and weighted scorecards'). The agent configured 'Initial Review' (2026-08-01..2026-10-15, Blind, Originality/Relevance/Comments) and a separate 'Final Review' round (2026-10-16..2026-11-30, Final Score 1-10 + Comments); the saved state screenshot shows both round cards with distinct names and distinct criteria and a 'Round saved' confirmation. Round names persisted beyond the page and beyond the scenario: the Assignments round selector and the Review Progress round selector both show 'Initial Review' in a later session. Slight evidence gap: the reloaded date values are not legible in the attached crops (the full-page shot was clipped), so date persistence rests on the agent's recorded observation rather than a readable screenshot.
evidence_refs: obs: Evaluation Plan editor supports blind review, date ranges, weighted rating criteria, select options, text criteria, and per-round reviewer pools. Initial Review configured with dates, blind mode... Final Review configured with dates and Final Score 1-10 plus Comments

items.reasoning: Reviewer membership is scoped inside each round card: the 'REVIEWER POOL' checkbox group (Ada Reviewer, Linus Reviewer, Sam Whitfield — Sam checked) sits within the Initial Review card, directly above 'Save round', with the Final Review card starting below it with its own name/blind/date fields. The Assignments page reinforces per-round scoping ('Add a reviewer directly to the selected round') as does Review Progress ('Counts cover this round only — assignments in other rounds are excluded'). The Final Review round's own pool contents are not visible in the attached crop, but the scoping is clearly per-round rather than global.
evidence_refs: obs: Evaluation Plan editor supports ... per-round reviewer pools

items.reasoning: The scorecard editor exposes a criterion type selector with 'Rating' (with min/max and weight) and 'Text', plus select/option support (the agent filled an options field with Accept/Maybe/Reject and the agent recorded that select options are supported). On the reviewer side all three types rendered and were filled: two numeric fields (4 and 2), a free-text comment, and a dropdown where 'Accept' was selected, after which submission succeeded and the item left the queue. Stored values were confirmed organizer-side (Originality 4, Relevance 2, exact comment text, normalized 3.33). Gap: the stored value of the dropdown (Accept) was not explicitly re-displayed in the recorded organizer detail observation, and the editor exhibited a bug where removing the default Recommendation criterion lost its editable options.
evidence_refs: obs: Results detail for Taming exposes stored review math: prior Sam review 4.00 normalized (Originality 4, Relevance 4) and new Sam review 3.33 normalized (Originality 4, Relevance 2), with exact comment

items.reasoning: Weights are first-class in the scorecard editor: Originality (Rating) carries weight 2 and Relevance (Rating) weight 1, and both values are still shown after 'Round saved'. The aggregate arithmetic matches weighted math: the new review of 'Taming 40-Minute CI' (Originality 4, Relevance 2) is stored as 3.33 normalized — i.e. (4·2 + 2·1)/3 — not the plain average 3.0; combined with the earlier all-4s review (4.00) the results table shows 3.67 across 2 reviews, which is the mean of 3.33 and 4.00.
evidence_refs: obs: Results detail for Taming exposes stored review math: prior Sam review 4.00 normalized ... new Sam review 3.33 normalized (Originality 4, Relevance 2)

items.reasoning: The organizer selected round 'Initial Review' + reviewer 'Sam Whitfield' and assigned exactly two submissions; the confirmation panel lists '2 of 2 selected assigned to Sam Whitfield — Taming 40-Minute CI → Sam Whitfield' and 'Your AI Pair Programmer → Sam Whitfield', with 'Docs That Answer Back' left unassigned. On the reviewer side, Sam's queue contained exactly those two items and not 'Docs That Answer Back', and became empty after both were scored — so the queue is assignment-scoped, not a global submission list.
evidence_refs: obs: Queue lists exactly two assigned submissions: Taming 40-Minute CI... and Your AI Pair Programmer...; unassigned Docs That Answer Back is absent

items.reasoning: The Assignments toolbar offers a 'Per-reviewer limit' field (value 5), an 'Auto-distribute' action, 'Select all' bulk selection with a running 'x of 9 selected' counter, and a track column on the selectable list. The agent exercised the round/reviewer/limit path and the bulk 'Assign selected' action successfully ('2 of 2 selected assigned to Sam Whitfield'), so scale tooling exists and functions rather than one-at-a-time-only assignment.
evidence_refs: obs: Assignments supports per-reviewer limit (default 5) and Auto-distribute. Initial Review selected, Sam Whitfield selected. Exactly two requested submissions assigned

items.reasoning: A per-round 'Blind review' selector exists (Initial Review set to 'Blind'; the Final Review card shows 'Identity visible', proving it is per-round). The reviewer's page for 'Taming 40-Minute CI' displayed 'Blind review — author identity redacted' and the agent scanned it and found none of 'Priya Raman', 'Marcus Okafor', or the company name. The organizer's submissions view of the same submission shows 'Priya Raman + Marcus Okafor', giving the required contrast.
evidence_refs: obs: Taming review page explicitly says 'Blind review — author identity redacted'; visible content contains no Priya Raman, Marcus Okafor, or company identity
turn 13 (ABS-S2, selected Blind for Initial Review)

items.reasoning: Review Progress ('Live completion by round and reviewer') lists per-reviewer counts and percentages scoped to the selected round. Baseline before the new reviews: 'Initial Review · 6 assigned · 1 complete · 3 reviewers' with 'Sam Whitfield 1 of 3 complete · 33%'. After Sam submitted both evaluations the same view reads '6 assigned · 3 complete' and 'Sam Whitfield 3 of 3 complete · 100%'. The absolute numbers differ from the rubric's 2/0 → 2/2 only because of a pre-seeded third assignment/review; the delta exactly matches the two evaluations submitted, so the counts track real state.
evidence_refs: obs: Organizer Review Progress shows Sam Whitfield 3 of 3 complete, 100% (not 2 of 2, because seeded prior assignment/review is included)

items.reasoning: The Review Progress header carries a 'Remind outstanding reviewers' bulk action targeting the lagging reviewers (Sam at 1 of 3, Ada 0 of 2, Linus 0 of 1). Triggering it produced an explicit success report: an inline panel and toast reading '3 reminder(s) logged'. (The agent's note that no confirmation appeared is contradicted by its own screenshot.)

The Results table shows a per-submission aggregate ('Score … / 5 normalized') plus review counts: 'Your AI Pair Programmer' 5.00 (1 review) and 'Taming 40-Minute CI' 3.67 (2 reviews), consistent with the entered scores including the earlier all-4s review. Toggling the sort control reorders rows correctly in both directions: descending puts 5.00 above 3.67, ascending puts 3.67 first, with unscored rows kept last as documented.
evidence_refs: obs: Organizer Results table ... Your AI Pair Programmer 5.00/5 normalized, 1 review ... Taming 40-Minute CI 3.67/5 normalized, 2 reviews

items.reasoning: Co-author capture works with role labels at submission time: the public form has a 'Co-authors / co-presenters' block with name/email/role (Co-author selected), and the pre-submit review step renders 'Co-author — Marcus Okafor · sbek-speaker2@example.com'. Marcus also persists into the organizer side, where the submissions/review inbox shows 'Priya Raman + Marcus Okafor' for Taming. Two gaps: the organizer-side view shows only concatenated names with no role label, and the speaker's saved submission detail/edit view no longer shows any participants section after save, so role/co-author data is not visible on the persisted speaker-side detail.
evidence_refs: obs: Submission detail/edit view for Taming 40-Minute CI showed proposal fields but no participants/co-author section after save

items.reasoning: A recusal control is present in the reviewer's scoring view with the recorded wording 'Declare conflict / recuse', and the organizer Assignments page has a corresponding 'RECUSED ASSIGNMENTS — Reviewers who declared a conflict. Reinstate returns the work to their queue' section, showing the flow is wired end-to-end. The control was not exercised, but the rubric awards pass for a present control with recorded wording.
evidence_refs: obs: Conflict control is present with exact wording 'Declare conflict / recuse'

items.reasoning: The Results page ('Human review aggregates and disposition') has an 'Export CSV' button; the agent triggered it and the page reported success: 'CSV download started — check your downloads folder.' No error state appeared.

The clone does claim AI-assisted review ('AI review assistance is advisory. Open any submission in Review Studio and choose AI draft review; a human must edit and submit it' on the Evaluation Plan, and a similar banner on Results; reviewer queue says 'AI drafts never decide'), so the item is in scope. However the agent never opened Review Studio to invoke 'AI draft review', so there is no evidence of an AI-generated numeric score with reasoning, no evidence of AI-vs-human distinction in results, and no override/persistence test. Its note that 'AI score/override was not present' was based only on the Results table, not on searching the documented entry point — insufficient to conclude the capability is absent or broken.
evidence_refs: obs: AI score/override was not present for these reviewed submissions; AI is labeled advisory

defects.description: Speaker-side submission detail/edit view drops the participants/co-author section after save: 'Marcus Okafor · Co-author' is shown in the pre-submit review and confirmation but is absent when the saved submission is reopened for viewing/editing, so the submitter can neither verify nor edit co-authors post-submission.

Scorecard editor bug: removing the default 'Recommendation' criterion from a round also removed its editable options, and the organizer could not re-create the requested Accept/Maybe/Reject dropdown on the Initial Review round (the criterion ended up absent there while the Final Review round retained its default Recommendation).
defects.where: Organizer → Evaluation Plan → round scorecard criteria editor

defects.description: Organizer submissions/review inbox shows co-participants as a concatenated name string ('Priya Raman + Marcus Okafor') with no role label, losing the Co-author/Co-presenter distinction captured at submission time.

Duplicate proposals for the same title are silently accepted, producing two 'Taming 40-Minute CI' rows (one scheduled/seeded, one newly submitted) in the speaker dashboard and organizer lists, with the seeded scheduled item not editable/reusable from the speaker portal.
Stale event context label: after switching the workspace to 'DevFlow Conf 2027' the sidebar footer still reads 'AI Engineer Summit · in-memory demo', which is misleading about which event is active.
defects.where: Organizer shell footer / event switcher (Settings page after switch)

areas.notes: Seeded fixture data shifted several baselines from the rubric's expected numbers (Sam already had a third, completed Initial Review assignment; 'Taming' already carried an all-4s review), so progress read 1-of-3 → 3-of-3 rather than 0-of-2 → 2-of-2 and the Taming aggregate read 3.67 across 2 reviews rather than 3.33 across 1. The rubric explicitly allows judging arithmetic including the earlier review, and the deltas are internally consistent, so these were treated as pass. One agent observation (no reminder confirmation) is contradicted by its own screenshot showing '3 reminder(s) logged'; the screenshot was taken as authoritative. ABS-14 is unjudgeable because the agent never entered Review Studio, the app's documented AI-draft entry point, even though the app advertises AI review assistance.

scenarios.scenarioName: Speaker seeds submissions with a co-author
scenarios.summary: Reopened closed CFP, submitted Taming with Marcus as Co-author, submitted Docs fresh, reused seeded rejected AI proposal. Captured co-author form/review/confirmation, dashboard, and Taming detail screenshots. Dashboard shows required titles/statuses but duplicate Taming seeded+new; saved detail omits participant list.
observations: CFP was initially closed; organizer Settings allowed moving close date to 2027-04-30 and saving, after which public CFP showed Open. Public form explicitly supports co-authors/co-presenters with name, email, and role (Co-presenter/Co-author). Filled Priya Raman + Marcus Okafor as Co-author and captured screenshots before review and on confirmation.

Speaker dashboard after submissions shows statuses: scheduled seeded Taming session, submitted Docs, submitted Taming (new reference), and rejected AI Pair Programmer—four visible entries, with duplicate Taming title because the seeded scheduled item was not editable/reusable from the dashboard. The required three unique proposal titles are present, but dashboard count is not exactly three.

Submission detail/edit view for Taming 40-Minute CI showed proposal fields but no participants/co-author section after save; co-author was visible in the pre-submit review and confirmation state, but not in the later edit detail. This is a product inconsistency affecting verification of participant persistence.

areas.title: AI Agenda & Schedule Builder

items.reasoning: The Schedule builder renders room lanes (Main Stage, Room 2A, Room 2B, Workshop Lab, Overflow Room) with a drop-hour selector, an unscheduled accepted-session pool, and List/Day/Week/Track/Room view toggles; sessions render as cards positioned by time and room (e.g. 'Room 2A · 10:00 AM–10:45 AM · Priya Raman (manual)' and 'Room 2B · 2:00 PM–2:45 PM · Your AI Pair Programmer…'). The agent observed three day tabs plus a day selector in the placement dialog offering the event days. Caveat noted as a defect: the day tabs shown after reload (Tue May 11 – Thu May 13 2027) do not match the day options offered at placement time (Oct 12/13 2026), so the day dimension is internally inconsistent.
evidence_refs: obs: Builder has Day/List/Week/Track/Room views, 3 day tabs, drop-time selector, unscheduled accepted-session pool

items.reasoning: Organizer added a room ('Overflow Room', capacity 200) via the '+ Room' control and it immediately appears as a schedulable lane in the grid ('Overflow Room seats 200' with a drop target) and as a selectable Room option in the placement dialog / AI draft placements. A track ('Community') was created via '+ Track' with a 'Track added' toast, and tracks are usable/visible: the New session form has a Track select, pool cards carry track badges (Engineering, AI Engineering, Developer Experience), and the public itinerary exposes a TRACK (3) filter with 'Track · Engineering' on a session card. The four fixture rooms (Main Stage, Room 2A, Room 2B, Workshop Lab) were present as lanes.
evidence_refs: obs: Existing fixture rooms Main Stage, Room 2A, Room 2B, Workshop Lab were present; added Overflow Room (capacity 200) and Community track successfully

items.reasoning: Click-to-assign placement works and persists: the session was placed via the 'Place …' dialog choosing Day / Start time / Room (10:00, Room 2A) and its card renders in the Room 2A lane at 10:00–10:45 with its title. After reload, Recent Placements ('Saved on the schedule — these survive a reload') still lists Priya Raman (manual) · 2026-10-12 · 10:00–10:45 · Room 2A, plus the two other placements. The exact fixture title 'Taming 40-Minute CI' was not in the accepted pool for this event (it appears only as a pre-existing placement in Main Hall), so a stand-in accepted session was used — the placement + persistence capability is nevertheless clearly demonstrated. Deduction of confidence because the persisted day (Oct 12 2026) does not correspond to the day tabs rendered after reload (May 11–13 2027), and the post-reload grid itself was not captured.
evidence_refs: obs: Reload retained all three placements

items.reasoning: Attempting to place the second Priya Raman session at the same 10:00 slot (different room, Room 2B) produced an immediate, in-dialog conflict panel naming the speaker: 'Speaker double-booked: Priya Raman is already speaking during this time.' with 'Pick a different time or room above, then submit again — nothing was changed.' The warning appeared at save time without a manual refresh and identified the double-booked speaker.
evidence_refs: obs: exact warning 'Speaker double-booked: Priya Raman is already speaking during this time.' and blocked save

items.reasoning: Placing a second session into Day 1 10:00 in the already-occupied Room 2A was rejected at placement time with an explicit room-conflict message: 'Room already booked: Room 2A is already occupied 10:00–10:45 by Priya Raman (manual).' and the note that nothing was changed — i.e. the overlap was prevented, satisfying the 'blocked' branch of the criterion.
evidence_refs: obs: Attempting Docs at 10:00 Room 2A produced exact warning 'Room already booked: Room 2A is already occupied 10:00–10:45 by Priya Raman (manual).' and blocked save

items.reasoning: Conflicts were resolved and the resulting placements persisted: the Pair session was rescheduled to 14:00 in Room 2B (card renders there with no conflict indicator) and the Docs session went to Oct 13 11:00 Room 2B, with all three placements intact after reload. A 'Move' control exists on each scheduled card. However, the evidence does not show an already-scheduled session being moved to a different slot/room — both 'resolutions' were performed by changing the time inside the placement dialog before the first successful save (the conflicting attempts were blocked, so nothing was ever scheduled in the conflicting slot). Therefore the move-an-existing-placement path and the clearing of a persisted conflict flag remain unverified.
evidence_refs: obs: Moving Pair to 14:00 cleared speaker conflict; placing Docs on Tue Oct 13 11:00 Room 2B succeeded. Reload retained all three placements

items.reasoning: A 'Publish agenda' action exists in the builder toolbar; after triggering it the page reports published status ('Published · 6 sessions') with an 'Open public itinerary' link, and the public surface at /public/events/evt-devflow-conf-2027/itinerary (banner 'Public program · no login') shows the scheduled fixture/stand-in sessions with day, time and room — e.g. Priya Raman (manual) Mon Oct 12 10:00–10:45 Room 2A, and the AI-accepted Thu May 13 placements (Lightning Q&A 3:00–3:45 Main Stage, Dana 3:45–4:30 Main Stage, Docs 3:45–4:30 Overflow Room), '6 of 6 sessions'. Handoff to the attendee-facing view is confirmed; rendering quality not graded here.
evidence_refs: obs: Publish agenda completed and reload confirms status: 'Published · 6 sessions' with Open public itinerary link
obs: Public itinerary opened in a new tab ... reachable without organizer login

items.reasoning: The builder contains an 'AI Agenda · advisory — Heuristic schedule assistant' with 'Generate draft' plus tunable parameters (day start/end hour, slot minutes, break minutes). One click generated a persisted draft with three proposed placements including day/time/room and reasons ('earliest conflict-free Main Stage slot; respected 45-minute duration, room, track, speaker overlap…'); 'Accept all' then wrote all three into the live schedule (Recent Placements show Lightning Q&A Thu May 13 3:00–3:45 Main Stage, Docs 3:45–4:30 Overflow Room, Dana 3:45–4:30 Main Stage, each marked 'AI accepted') and the unscheduled pool emptied. That is one-action assisted placement of previously unscheduled sessions.
evidence_refs: obs: Generate draft succeeded ... 3 proposed placements
obs: Accept all succeeded ... each marked AI accepted. Pool is empty

defects.description: Event-day / date inconsistency in the schedule builder: for DevFlow Conf 2027 (event days Tue May 11 – Thu May 13 2027, as shown by the day tabs after reload and by the AI draft output), the 'Place session' dialog offered days 'Mon · Oct 12, 2026' and 'Tue · Oct 13, 2026', and the resulting placements persisted on those 2026 dates. The result is a schedule where manually placed sessions sit outside the event's own day range, and the public itinerary lists five unrelated day tabs (Oct 12–13 2026 plus May 11–13 2027) for one three-day event.
defects.where: /app/schedule — Place session dialog, day tabs, Recent Placements; public itinerary day tabs

defects.description: Stale/cross-event data on the schedule page after switching events: immediately after switching the workspace selector from 'AI Engineer Summit' to 'DevFlow Conf 2027', the page still showed the identical Recent Placement 'Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale · Mon · Oct 12 · 9:00 AM–9:45 AM · Main Hall' and the same speaker list, suggesting the schedule view does not fully re-scope to the newly selected event until further interaction.

An interactive control in the builder was unclickable during session creation (click timed out on the element, forcing the agent to re-snapshot and use an alternate control), indicating a transiently non-interactive/overlapped button in the New session / pool area.

areas.notes: Both scenarios completed. The clone implements a click-to-assign (plus advertised drag) room-lane builder with server-side hard conflict blocking, room/track creation, persistence, a heuristic 'AI Agenda' auto-placer, publish, and a no-login public itinerary — a strong functional match for this area. Two evidence limitations: the specified fixture proposals ('Taming 40-Minute CI' as an unscheduled item, the second Priya session) were not in the DevFlow accepted pool, so the agent created manual accepted stand-ins (functionally equivalent for judging placement/conflict behavior), and the post-reload grid itself (as opposed to the persisted Recent Placements list) was not captured. AIA-06 is partial only because no already-scheduled session was actually moved via the existing 'Move' control; conflicts were avoided at placement time because the app blocks conflicting saves outright.

areas.title: Call for Papers

items.reasoning: The public form clearly renders a mix of field types with required flags and enforces validation: 'Session title *' (short text), 'Abstract *' (long text) and the newly added 'Audience level *' dropdown (Beginner shown, options Beginner/Intermediate/Advanced per the builder observation), and an empty submit produced inline errors plus a toast 'Missing: Session title is required, Abstract is required, Speaker bio is required'. Gap: the builder work only demonstrably added a dropdown and renamed/configured the conditional field; no added short-text field ('Key takeaway') exists — CFP-S2 explicitly searched the whole proposal form and found none — and the builder screenshot showing the added fields/required flags was not attached, so field-addition breadth across 3 types is not fully proven.
evidence_refs: obs: Added Audience level dropdown with Beginner/Intermediate/Advanced and renamed conditional Workshop plan to Workshop prerequisites; Speaker bio was set required
obs: no visible 'Key takeaway' field anywhere in the proposal form

items.reasoning: Two independent scenarios exercised the format-dependent field. CFP-S1 selected 'Workshop (120 min)' then 'Talk (30 min)' and observed the 'Workshop prerequisites' and duration fields appear immediately and disappear immediately without reload; CFP-S2 repeated the toggle. The public form itself advertises the behaviour ('Tip: choose Workshop format to reveal workshop-specific fields'). The attached before/after screenshots are cropped above the conditional field, so visual proof is indirect, but the observations plus the app's own copy are consistent in both directions.
evidence_refs: obs: Workshop prerequisites and duration appeared immediately when Format changed to Workshop and disappeared immediately when changed to Talk, without full page reload

items.reasoning: The portal at /e/ai-engineer-summit/cfp loads with no login (reached in a fresh tab and again from the marketing home in CFP-S2) and shows the event name 'AI Engineer Summit', a visible window 'Accepting until 4/30/2027, 12:00:00 AM · max 10 per user · Open', the track list 'AI Engineering · Platform & Infra · Developer Experience', and a Track dropdown plus Format dropdown offering Talk (30 min) / Workshop (120 min) matching the fixture vocabulary.

The organizer Settings page exposes a CFP window with open/close datetimes and 'Close CFP now'; after closing, the logged-out public portal shows a 'Closed' pill, heading 'Submissions closed' and 'Submissions closed. The deadline was 8/12/2026, 4:33:31 AM.' with no name/email inputs, Continue button or any way to start a submission — a clear contrast with the earlier open state.
evidence_refs: obs: Logged-out public CFP explicitly shows Closed and 'Submissions closed'; no name/email inputs or Continue/new submission control

items.reasoning: The portal's step '1. YOU' collects submitter name/email to establish the submitter identity (the app is an explicitly credential-free persona demo), the 'Taming 40-Minute CI' proposal submitted successfully with an on-screen confirmation ('Submitted' pill, 'Proposal received', reference sub-0a677221), and the speaker portal 'My submissions' page later lists both of Priya's proposals with status labels. Weakness: /p/talks was intermittently broken during CFP-S2 (stuck on 'Loading…' / home content), so the immediately-post-submission 'Submitted' row was not observed; the working list was captured later with post-decision statuses.
evidence_refs: obs: Both complete proposals were submitted successfully with status 'Submitted' confirmation

items.reasoning: Submitted data clearly reaches the organizer side: the organizer Assignments table lists both fixture proposals with speaker 'Priya Raman', tracks 'AI Engineering' and 'Platform & Infra' and status 'submitted', the organizer submissions list showed both titles with decisions, and the abstract text is stored verbatim (visible, unmangled, including the appended sentence, with 'Category: Platform & Infra'). Gap: no attached organizer submission-detail screenshot, and the custom 'Audience level' value (and format) were never shown in an organizer detail view, so full custom-field round-trip is unverified.
evidence_refs: obs: Submissions list now shows side-by-side decisions: Taming 40-Minute CI — Accepted (score 4), Your AI Pair Programmer... — Rejected

items.reasoning: With only the session title entered, the speaker used a save-draft action that produced a persistent resume URL (?submission=sub-0a677221&token=...) and a draft indicator was captured; navigating back to that URL later re-opened the form with the saved title (and subsequently entered data) pre-filled, i.e. the draft resumes. The draft-indicator screenshot itself is not attached, but the URL change, the agent's observation and the pre-filled resume page corroborate it.
evidence_refs: obs: Public CFP supports draft saving, conditional workshop fields, required validation...

items.reasoning: The speaker re-opened the submission via its resume link while the CFP was open, appended the sentence, and the review step showed the abstract ending exactly 'Updated: now includes 2026 benchmark data.'. The edit persisted server-side across sessions: in a separate scenario the reviewer's read-only view of the same submission renders the abstract ending with that identical sentence, and the organizer-side review studio was opened on the same record. Only caveat: no dedicated organizer-detail screenshot of the abstract was attached, so the propagation is evidenced via the reviewer rendering of the same stored abstract.
evidence_refs: obs: Review displayed abstract ending exactly 'Updated: now includes 2026 benchmark data.' before resubmission

items.reasoning: The organizer Assignments page has an 'Invite reviewer' form; inviting Sam Whitfield produced a confirmation panel with a usable reviewer access link (explicitly credential-free demo persona access), the agent used that link and landed on a reviewer shell whose navigation is only 'My queue / Completed / Guidelines' with the persona 'Sam Whitfield · reviewer' — no organizer/admin navigation (Submissions, Assignments, Settings, etc.) is exposed.

The reviewer scorecard was filled with 4/5 ratings and the fixture comment ('Strong practical content and a clear narrative arc; ... Recommend accept for the Platform track.'), submission produced the toast 'Evaluation submitted' and the item moved to 'Completed reviews' with a 'Done' badge; the organizer's Review Studio for that submission shows Sam Whitfield's Overall rating 4, relevance 4, novelty 4, recommendation Accept and the exact comment text, and the submissions list shows score 4.
evidence_refs: obs: Organizer Review Studio visibly shows Sam Whitfield's submitted review: Overall rating 4, Program relevance 4, Novelty 4, Recommendation Accept, and the exact comment text
obs: Submissions list now shows ... Accepted (score 4)

items.reasoning: The organizer opened each submission detail and used the decision controls, after which the submissions list shows the two proposals with distinct statuses — 'Taming 40-Minute CI — Accepted (score 4)' and 'Your AI Pair Programmer... — Rejected'. The list screenshot itself is not attached, but the observation is specific and is corroborated downstream by the speaker portal ('Rejected' badge on the AI talk, scheduled session for the CI talk) and by the accepted talk becoming placeable on the schedule.
evidence_refs: obs: Submissions list now shows side-by-side decisions: Taming 40-Minute CI — Accepted (score 4), Your AI Pair Programmer... — Rejected

items.reasoning: Signed in as Priya Raman after decisions, the speaker portal 'My submissions' page shows 'Your AI Pair Programmer Is Lying to You...' with a red 'Rejected' badge and 'Taming 40-Minute CI...' with a 'Scheduled' badge plus 'Organizer-linked session · 9:00 AM–9:45 AM Main Hall'; the home page also shows 'Your session' for the accepted talk and a decision message. 'Scheduled' is an unambiguous post-acceptance state rather than the literal word 'Accepted', a minor wording deviation.
evidence_refs: obs: Priya speaker portal home shows the accepted session ... and latest rejection message

items.reasoning: Per the item's auto-partial rule only the UI-observable half is judged. The organizer Comms area exists and, per the agent's inspection, logs both decision emails as sent (mock mailer) — an acceptance message for 'Taming 40-Minute CI' and a rejection for 'Your AI Pair Programmer' — with per-recipient entries, timestamps, rendered bodies and ICS links; the speaker portal correspondingly shows the decision message body ('Update on your AI Engineer Summit proposal'). The default compose subject/body differs from the fixture text, the confirmation screenshot is not attached, and one navigation attempt to /app/comms rendered the Submissions inbox instead, so dispatch confirmation is credible but not fully demonstrated.
evidence_refs: obs: Comms page verifies both decision emails already sent (mock) ... with per-recipient log, timestamps, rendered bodies, and ICS links
obs: Attempted organizer Comms navigation (/app/comms), but URL changed while page remained the Submissions inbox

items.reasoning: After acceptance, the accepted proposal appeared on the organizer Schedule as a placeable session; the placement dialog was titled 'Place Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale' and only day/time/room were chosen (no re-typing of title/speaker/track). The resulting schedule entry carries title, speaker Priya Raman and track 'Platform & Infra' (Mon Oct 12, 9:00–9:45, Main Hall), and the speaker portal mirrors the same session as 'Organizer-linked session'.
evidence_refs: obs: Schedule confirms accepted talk placed: Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale, speaker Priya Raman, track Platform & Infra, Mon Oct 12 9:00–9:45 Main Hall

items.reasoning: With the close date in the past, the speaker's submissions page does surface a closed state ('CFP closed' indicator in the header of 'My submissions') and the accepted/scheduled proposal offers no edit affordance. However the rejected proposal still exposes a 'View or edit submission' button after close, and no attempt to open/save an edit in the closed state was captured, so the lock is only partially evidenced and an edit affordance remains visible.
evidence_refs: obs: no edit-lock form was reachable

items.reasoning: The organizer shell has an event switcher ('Organizer workspace: AI Engineer Summit ▾'); creating 'DevFlow Conf 2027' produced a confirmation card ('Created DevFlow Conf 2027 · slug devflow-conf-2027 · empty by design ... Switch to DevFlow Conf 2027 / Stay in AI Engineer Summit'), and the workspace header subsequently shows 'DevFlow Conf 2027' — both events coexist and are reachable via the switcher (the reviewer shell also has an event switcher).

With the workspace switched to 'DevFlow Conf 2027' the Submissions inbox renders 'No submissions — Nothing in the inbox yet', while the AI Engineer Summit workspace shows 5 submissions on the Command dashboard and populated lists. A second scenario independently confirmed DevFlow Conf 2027 has no submissions while the seeded proposals remain under AI Engineer Summit — no cross-event leakage observed.
evidence_refs: obs: Organizer selected DevFlow Conf 2027, but submissions list is empty; seeded proposals exist under AI Engineer Summit

defects.description: Speaker portal 'Talks' route is flaky/broken: it repeatedly rendered an indefinite 'Loading…' state or fell back to the Home content instead of the submissions list, preventing the speaker from seeing proposal statuses in two separate runs (it did eventually render correctly in CFP-S4).

Organizer 'Comms' navigation is unreliable: clicking it changed the URL to /app/comms while the page kept rendering the Submissions inbox, hiding the notification compose/send UI until a later attempt.

Speaker portal shows contradictory onboarding state: 'ONBOARDING 100%' with '0/0 required tasks complete' and 'All required tasks complete. You're clear.' while simultaneously displaying a red 'Not ready' badge.
Switching the demo persona to another speaker (Sam Rivera · speaker) renders an error banner 'speaker persona required' with an otherwise empty page.

After the CFP close date is in the past, the speaker's submissions page still exposes a 'View or edit submission' affordance for one proposal, which is inconsistent with the 'CFP closed' indicator shown on the same page.

A newly created event inherits some seeded/command-shell wording and defaults, and the CFP builder does not expose a way to add a plain short-text custom question (no 'Key takeaway'-style text field was findable anywhere in the form).

areas.notes: The clone is a deliberately credential-free 'persona simulation' demo (no real signup/login), so account creation for speakers/reviewers is modelled as name/email identity plus invite links; this was accepted as the app's own equivalent for CFP-05 and CFP-10. All four scenarios completed, so no criterion was blocked by the harness. Evidence weakness worth noting: several key organizer-side screenshots (CFP builder configured, submissions decisions list, submission detail, comms send log, schedule) were captured but not attached, so CFP-06, CFP-12 and CFP-14 rest partly on the agent's specific written observations, which are internally consistent with the attached reviewer/speaker/assignment screenshots. Depth items (blind review, weighted scorecards, exact queue scoping) visible in screenshots are owned by the abstract-management spec and were not scored here.

scenarios.scenarioName: Organizer builds and publishes the CFP
scenarios.summary: Built/published the seeded event CFP, added requested Audience level and conditional Workshop prerequisites, set close date, verified public logged-out form, live conditional toggling, empty-field validation, and created/probed second event with isolated empty submissions.
observations: Organizer shell is credential-free persona simulation; no signup/login was required. Existing seeded event was AI Engineer Summit, so DevFlow Conf 2027 was created as a second event. Created event defaults retained some command-shell wording but event-scoped submissions showed 0.

Configured and published CFP builder at /app/forms. Existing tracks and formats exactly matched fixtures. Added Audience level dropdown with Beginner/Intermediate/Advanced and renamed conditional Workshop plan to Workshop prerequisites; Speaker bio was set required. Conditional visibility is supported and toggled live without reload.
Exact public CFP URL: https://cue-program-ops.headley-max.workers.dev/e/ai-engineer-summit/cfp

Logged-out public CFP showed AI Engineer Summit, open status, deadline 4/30/2027, tracks and start form. Workshop prerequisites and duration appeared immediately when Format changed to Workshop and disappeared immediately when changed to Talk, without full page reload. Empty Review attempt produced required validation alerts for Session title, Abstract, and Speaker bio.

areas.title: Content Management & Speaker Deliverables

items.reasoning: The file-request task creator accepts task name, due date, instructions, accepted MIME types and per-speaker assignment; the filled form for "Upload Session Presentation" (due 05/01/2027, application/pdf) is shown, followed by a success banner "3 deliverables created · Upload Session Presentation · due 2027-05-01 · Assigned to: Priya Raman, Marcus Okafor, Dana Kowalski" and the filled headshot form (due 04/14/2027, image/png,image/jpeg). The resulting dashboard lists both tasks per speaker with the correct due dates and incomplete/draft status for Priya and Marcus.
evidence_refs: obs: Content > Deliverables supports task creation with due date, instructions, accepted MIME types, and All speakers assignment

items.reasoning: Priya's portal Deliverables page lists both assigned tasks with session, due dates (2027-05-01 / 2027-04-14), version counts, constraints and status chips (Incomplete / Complete). Uploading slides.pdf produced the inline confirmation "Uploaded slides.pdf as version 1", the file listed as slides.pdf v1 · Current against the presentation task/session, and the task badge flipped to Complete; the portal list afterwards shows the presentation task Complete with 2 version(s).
evidence_refs: obs: Upload succeeded: slides.pdf version 1 then re-upload created version 2 ... Task is Complete

items.reasoning: Scoping is evidenced: Priya's Deliverables page shows only her own session ("Taming 40-Minute CI") and states "Deliverables are scoped to the signed-in speaker", and no Marcus content is visible (Marcus is not even a selectable persona in that event). Direct /admin, /organizer and /dashboard navigations all redirected to the public root. However the app is explicitly persona-simulated with no authentication ("Identity is header/persona simulation — not multi-tenant auth") and the root page exposes a one-click Jordan Alvarez organizer shell; the actual organizer route (/app) was never tested from the speaker context, so organizer views are not demonstrably blocked for a speaker account — the tested routes appear simply not to exist.
evidence_refs: obs: Persona selector contains only six speaker personas and no Marcus Okafor

items.reasoning: After the second upload the speaker view lists "slides.pdf · 2 versions" with v2 · 8/12/2026 5:01:38 AM marked Current (with View) and v1 · 5:01:23 AM still individually viewable. The organizer Files library mirrors this with a VERSION HISTORY block showing v2 (Current, View) and v1 (View) with ISO timestamps.

Speaker view shows the comment "Draft deck - final version coming Friday." tagged Speaker · Priya Raman with a UTC timestamp. The organizer Files library shows the same thread on Priya's slides.pdf plus the organizer reply tagged Organizer · Jordan Alvarez · 2026-08-12 03:03:12 UTC ("Thanks - please confirm the final version by Tuesday.").

The upload control on the deliverable page states "Accepted: application/pdf · Maximum 2 MB. Re-uploading creates a new version.", and the portal list rows also repeat "application/pdf · max 2 MB" per task.
evidence_refs: obs: Presentation upload UI explicitly states accepted application/pdf, maximum 2 MB

items.reasoning: The organizer Deliverables dashboard lists every speaker-task pair with session, due date, version count and status chips; in S1 all newly created rows show incomplete/draft (Priya, Marcus, Dana). In S3 the dashboard reflects the upload state: Priya's presentation row shows complete/submitted with 2 upload version(s) while other rows remain incomplete/draft. A status filter select exists ("All deliverables" → "Incomplete") and was successfully applied per the transcript, though the filtered screenshot itself was not attached for visual confirmation; Marcus's rows could not be re-checked in S3 because that event roster differs.

A bulk "Remind outstanding speakers" action is clearly present on the deliverables dashboard next to the status filter and was invoked after filtering to Incomplete (transcript turn 10, followed by a reminder-confirmation screenshot). The agent reports 2 mock reminders were sent, but the confirmation screenshot was not attached, so the send-confirmation UI could not be visually verified; actual delivery is out of scope.

The session content editor exposes Title/Abstract fields and Save; the server-side change history subsequently reloaded in the editor records save #1 with the diff "Title: Taming 40-Minute CI… → UPDATED: Taming 40-Minute CI…" plus an abstract diff, and save #2 with a further abstract change, proving the edits were persisted server-side rather than held in local state. The final session list shows the reverted canonical title with "5 changes". A direct screenshot of the list/detail displaying the UPDATED prefix was not attached, so persistence is inferred from the persisted diff history rather than seen in the list.

The speaker content editor for Priya shows a save confirmation "Saved Priya Raman at 5:04:57 AM · Bio 379 characters · headshot stored · pushed to the roster and public projection", the bio textarea containing the appended sentence ("Priya leads the developer-productivity group at Latticework Systems."), and the uploaded headshot.png rendered as a decoded 256×256 image preview. No separate post-reload screenshot was attached, but the confirmation states the values were stored and pushed to the roster/public projection.

The session editor's "Change history" panel lists 3 timestamped saves, each attributed to Jordan Alvarez with field-level diffs and a "Restore this version" control; restoring produced the toast "Restored the version saved at 2026-08-12 05:03:40.206" and the panel state after restore shows the title diff reverted (entry #3 shows UPDATED → original). A later view shows 5 attributed entries.

An "Approval status" select (Draft/Approved/…) exists per session, persists (session list shows an "approved" badge and the editor confirms "Approval approved · saved … Approved sessions appear on the public page immediately"), and the approved "Taming 40-Minute CI" session appears on the public sessions catalog with its content. However the gate is not exclusive to approval: the session list shows "Shipping AI Products" and "Advanced Agents Workshop" with approval status draft, yet both appear in the public catalog (4 of 4 sessions), so unapproved content is not reliably excluded — the exclusions that do occur correlate with unscheduled sessions rather than approval state.

The Content > Files library aggregates uploads across sessions: Priya Raman · Taming 40-Minute CI · slides.pdf · uploaded 2026-08-12 · 2 versions with full version history, comments and an approval-state select; headshot.png and another session's slides.pdf are listed alongside with speaker/session/date/version metadata.

A "Generate ZIP · choose content" dialog offers Select all / Clear all, per-session checkboxes (6 sessions) and per-file checkboxes (3 files), a "Group folders by" selector, and states only current versions are archived. After selecting a file, the UI confirms "ZIP ready · download started · cue-content-archive.zip · 1 file · grouped by session" including the exact included filename, plus a toast. Archive contents themselves are for manual verification.

defects.description: Internal approval status does not gate the public catalog: sessions whose approval status is "draft" (Shipping AI Products, Advanced Agents Workshop) are rendered on the public Sessions page (4 of 4), so unapproved content is publicly visible; visibility appears driven by a separate public/scheduled flag instead.
defects.where: Organizer Content > Session & speaker editors vs public /e/ai-engineer-summit/public/sessions

defects.description: No real access control: identity is header/persona simulation, and the public root exposes a one-click organizer shell, so any visitor can reach organizer-only surfaces regardless of speaker context (self-disclosed "not multi-tenant auth").
defects.where: Landing page role/persona selector and /app/* organizer shell

defects.description: Duplicate/conflicting task surfaces in the speaker portal: /p/tasks shows a generic seeded list ("Upload headshot · Done", "Upload presentation slides · Pending", due 2026-10-01) that disagrees with the /p/deliverables list of the actual organizer-created file-request tasks (due 2027-05-01 / 2027-04-14), which can mislead speakers about deadlines and completion.

Inconsistent deliverable status rendering: Priya's "Upload Final Headshot" row displayed complete/submitted in one dashboard render and incomplete/submitted (with 1 upload version) in a later render of the same event, so the completion chip and upload state disagree.
Change history records no-op saves as entries ("#4/#5 … No field changes — Saved with no field changes"), cluttering the audit trail and its restore controls.

areas.notes: Continuity caveat: S1 was performed in a "DevFlow Conf 2027" workspace with a Priya/Marcus/Dana roster, while S2 and S3 operated on the seeded "AI Engineer Summit" workspace (no Marcus persona available), so cross-scenario chaining for Marcus's rows is inferred rather than directly observed. Several S3 screenshots referenced in the transcript (filtered deliverables dashboard, reminder confirmation, mid-scenario session list with the UPDATED title) were not attached, which limited confidence on CNT-07, CNT-08 and CNT-09; those verdicts lean on transcript actions plus adjacent attached evidence. Overall the clone implements the deliverables lifecycle unusually completely (file-request tasks, versioning, cross-role comments, files library, ZIP export with grouping, change history with restore); the weakest link is the approval gate on public output and the absence of real authentication.

scenarios.scenarioName: Organizer sets up content collection
scenarios.summary: Completed organizer content-collection setup in DevFlow Conf 2027. Captured screenshots of filled task forms, Marcus session editor, and full deliverables dashboard. Verified both requested tasks and due dates for Priya and Marcus, pending statuses, and accepted MIME handling. No separate upload-enable toggle found.
observations: Organizer shell is credential-free persona simulation. DevFlow Conf 2027 was pre-seeded and switched via event menu; roster includes Priya Raman, Marcus Okafor, and Dana. Marcus's existing manual session was edited to Lightning: Agents in Production Q&A, Lightning Talk (10 min), AI/Agents track, Approved; deliverables reflect the updated title.

Content > Deliverables supports task creation with due date, instructions, accepted MIME types, and All speakers assignment. Saved Upload Session Presentation (2027-05-01, PDF instructions) and Upload Final Headshot (print quality) (2027-04-14). Dashboard shows both tasks for Priya and Marcus with due dates and incomplete/pending statuses; it also includes Dana because All speakers means all 3 roster speakers.
No separate file-uploads enable toggle was found in Content or Settings during inspection; Content includes Files library and export controls. Settings focuses CFP/event basics and program structure.

areas.title: Speaker CRM (Cross-Event Speaker Database)

items.reasoning: A top-level 'Speaker CRM' nav item sits alongside (not inside) per-event modules and loads /app/crm titled 'Organization-level speaker directory across events — contacts, pipeline, segments, and import.' The directory shows a Contacts KPI of 11 → 14 after import, with contact records reachable at /app/crm/contacts/<id> showing name + email, and a Search box that the agent exercised with 'Priya' (obs: search worked, directory listed 14 contacts including Marcus, Priya, Dana). Confidence is medium only because the screenshots crop below the search bar so the narrowed row list itself is not visible; the agent's observation plus the profile/pipeline/import rows corroborate the data.
evidence_refs: obs: CRM import created 3 contacts with validation table; directory grew from 11 to 14. Search and company filter worked.
obs: Organizer shell has explicit top-level Speaker CRM navigation at /app/crm, distinct from per-event Speakers

items.reasoning: Beyond the text Search, the directory exposes attribute dropdown filters: Tag (All tags (19)), Company (All companies (10)) and Stage (All stages). The agent selected Company = 'Latticework Systems' and reported the filter narrowed results correctly; the 'All companies' option provides the clear path. Medium confidence because the filtered row list is cropped out of the screenshot, so narrowing/restoration is attested by the agent's observation rather than visible rows.
evidence_refs: obs: Search and company filter worked.

items.reasoning: The contact profile shows identity fields (name, email, 'Principal Engineer @ Latticework Systems', bio line), tags, an internal NOTES composer, an EVENT HISTORY panel and a timestamped STAGE TIMELINE. The note 'Met at DevFlow 2026...' saved with a confirmation and still renders on subsequent server-rendered views of the profile and in the org activity feed; on Marcus the note persisted across later page loads, and EVENT HISTORY populated with 'DevFlow Conf 2027 · speaker · accepted · spk-9538b289' after linking, satisfying the cross-event history surface.
evidence_refs: obs: Priya profile note persisted and activity feed showed it.

items.reasoning: The Segments page has a CUSTOM FIELD DEFINITIONS manager (field label, type Dropdown, options) with a defined 'Speaker Type' select (Internal, External). On Priya's profile the CUSTOM FIELDS panel exposes 'Speaker Type (dropdown)' and the agent set it to External; an ad-hoc field (AI=yes) and tags are also supported. The agent observed both the External value and the ad-hoc field persisted.
evidence_refs: obs: custom dropdown Speaker Type Internal/External existed and External persisted; ad-hoc AI=yes also persisted

items.reasoning: An Import contacts entry point exists with both a 'Choose File' CSV upload control and a paste area, a Validate step that renders a per-row table (row / name / email / status 'would_create'), and an Import that reported 'Created 3, merged 0, skipped 0' with new contact ids. Contacts KPI moved 11 → 14 and the three imported people (Priya Raman, Marcus Okafor, Dana Kowalski, tagged 'imported') subsequently appear in the CRM data (pipeline cards, activity feed, contact profiles). Medium confidence because the agent's file-upload attempt hit a stale-ref harness error and it pasted the same CSV content instead, so the file-picker path itself was not exercised.
evidence_refs: obs: CRM import created 3 contacts with validation table; directory grew from 11 to 14.

items.reasoning: Profiles show a 'POSSIBLE DUPLICATES — Same name or email as this contact' panel with Open / 'Merge into this' actions (visible on Marcus). For the test the agent created Priya Raman with an alternate email, the panel flagged it immediately, and 'Merge into this' collapsed the pair into the chosen record (the one merged into = primary), logging 'Merged duplicate Priya Raman <priya.raman@sbek-test.example.com>' in the activity feed; the Contacts KPI returned to 14 (15 after creation, 14 after merge), consistent with a single surviving record. Gap: no side-by-side comparison / field-level value selection screen, and the post-merge directory rows were not screenshotted.
evidence_refs: obs: profile immediately showed Possible duplicates by same name ... No side-by-side comparison screen was offered.

items.reasoning: 'Sourcing pipeline' at /app/crm/pipeline is a kanban board with stage columns Prospect, Contacted, Invited, Confirmed (visible) plus Alumni and Declined (observed), covering the open→won/lost lifecycle. An 'Add prospect' picker enrolled Marcus Okafor from the directory with a 'Contact enrolled as prospect' toast and column counts updating (Prospect 5→4 / Contacted 1→2). Stage moves are made via per-card stage buttons; Marcus moved prospect→contacted→invited and the stage persisted on subsequent freshly loaded pages (profile shows stage 'invited' with a timestamped timeline; org activity feed lists both moves). Drag-and-drop is absent and no score/rationale at enrollment, neither of which is required.
evidence_refs: obs: Sourcing pipeline exists at /app/crm/pipeline with stage columns Prospect, Contacted, Invited, Confirmed, Alumni, Declined.

items.reasoning: Opening the pipeline contact detail exposes a NOTES composer; the note 'Left voicemail 2027-01-15; follow up next week.' saved with confirmation and still renders (author + timestamp) on the later server-rendered view of the same profile after further navigation/actions. The STAGE TIMELINE lists the transitions performed in the scenario with timestamps ('contacted → invited 5:22:33', 'prospect → contacted 5:22:22', '— → prospect 5:19:54', later 'invited → confirmed 5:22:53'), and the org activity feed mirrors them.
evidence_refs: obs: Marcus detail persisted internal note ... and stage timeline

items.reasoning: A Segments area exists ('Saved filters for outreach and pipeline lists') with a 'Save segment' form (name + stage + tag) and saved segments listed with member counts — 'Confirmed speakers 5 contacts' and 'AI Experts 3 contacts' — each with an 'Open in directory' action. However the AI Experts segment was pre-seeded rather than created from a filtered view during the run, and the agent never clicked 'Open in directory' to show the reopened member list, so the save→reopen-with-members round trip is unverified. The save form is also detached from the directory filter state (it re-specifies stage/tag) and offers no dynamic/curated type choice.
evidence_refs: obs: Segment area already contained AI Experts (3 contacts) plus Confirmed speakers

items.reasoning: The push-to-event capability is present and appears to work at the CRM side: the profile header has an event picker (which offered 'DevFlow Conf 2027'), a role selector ('Speaker') and an 'Add to event' button; after use the page shows 'Linked speaker: Marcus Okafor · spk-9538b289 · DevFlow Conf 2027' and EVENT HISTORY renders 'DevFlow Conf 2027 · speaker · accepted · spk-9538b289'. But the criterion's confirmation inside the target event's speakers module was never shown: the event switcher click was blocked by an overlay, the /app/speakers roster screenshotted remained AI Engineer Summit's (no Marcus), and the agent explicitly noted no event speaker roster for Marcus was surfaced. Also inconsistent state was reported (Event history sometimes still 'No linked events yet') plus repeated 'Already linked to event' toasts.
evidence_refs: obs: Add-to-event action offered DevFlow Conf 2027 and returned 'Already linked to event' / confirmed state; ... CRM detail's Event history remained 'No linked events yet' and no separate event speaker roster for Marcus was surfaced.

items.reasoning: UI-observable half satisfied: selecting 2 directory contacts turned the header action into 'Communicate (2)', which opened a 'Bulk communicate' modal stating '2 recipient(s)' and listing merge tags ({{name}}, {{first_name}}, {{company}}, {{event_name}}) with Subject and Body fields. After 'Send now' the Campaigns KPI went 0 → 1 and the activity feed logged a 'campaign' entry ('Speak at DevFlow Conf 2027? · 2 recipient(s)') plus per-recipient notes 'Email sent: ... (mock_sent)'; Campaign history page lists the campaign with subject/body. Gap (non-blocking): no preview with resolved personalization — the stored body keeps the raw {{name}} token.
evidence_refs: obs: Bulk Communicate exists ... campaign history shows 1 campaign, 2 recipients, and per-recipient recent activity entries (mock_sent).

items.reasoning: The CRM landing (/app/crm) is an org-level overview with KPI cards — CONTACTS 14, SEGMENTS 2, CAMPAIGNS 0→1, TOP TAG (with 'Filter by this tag →' drill-through) — plus a populated 'CONTACTS BY STAGE' bar widget (Prospect/Contacted/Invited/Confirmed/Alumni/Declined counts) and a RECENT ACTIVITY feed. The Contacts KPI of 14 matches the directory row count the agent observed. Medium confidence: there is no dedicated analytics page with company/region/source breakdowns (the agent noted /app/crm/overview falls back to the landing page), so the analytics surface is limited to the stage distribution and activity feed.
evidence_refs: obs: Contacts KPI 14 matches the 14 visible directory contacts. /app/crm/overview fell back to landing page.

defects.description: Cross-event linkage is not reflected in the target event's speaker roster surface: after 'Add to event' created 'Linked speaker: Marcus Okafor · spk-9538b289 · DevFlow Conf 2027', no event-level speaker list for that contact was surfaced, and the agent reported the CRM profile's Event history at times still read 'No linked events yet' despite the link succeeding — inconsistent state between the link record, event history panel, and directory event count.

Clicking the event switcher was blocked because the DevFlow Conf 2027 option button overlaid the target control, and Escape did not dismiss the layer, making event switching unreliable from the CRM page.

'Add to event' also silently advanced the contact's pipeline stage to 'confirmed' and fired duplicate 'Already linked to event' toasts stacked on screen, which is misleading feedback for an idempotent action.
Merge flow offers no side-by-side comparison or field-level value selection; merging is a single 'Merge into this' action with no preview of what data will win.
defects.where: CRM contact detail → POSSIBLE DUPLICATES panel

defects.description: Bulk communicate stores/sends the raw merge tokens with no resolved-personalization preview; campaign history shows the body still containing '{{name}}', so organizers cannot verify substitution.
defects.where: CRM Bulk communicate modal / Campaign history

defects.description: Directory appears to retain multiple same-name contacts (several 'Priya Raman' cards from different records visible across pipeline stages) without a consolidated duplicate resolution prompt at the directory level.

areas.notes: The clone implements the optional Speaker CRM area substantially: org-level Speaker CRM nav with directory + KPI landing, dropdown filters, CSV validate/import, custom field definitions, tags, notes with activity log, duplicate detection/merge, kanban sourcing pipeline with timestamped stage timeline, segments, bulk mock-mailer campaigns with history, and an add-to-event action. Evidence limitations to note (not app defects): screenshots crop the directory table rows so search/filter narrowing rests on the agent's observations; the CSV was pasted rather than uploaded via the file picker after a stale-ref tool error; the agent never opened a saved segment's member list; and the DevFlow Conf 2027 event roster was never inspected because the event switcher was overlaid, leaving CRM-10 verification incomplete.

scenarios.scenarioName: Build and organize the speaker database
scenarios.summary: Completed CRM scenario with org-level Speaker CRM, CSV validation/import of Priya/Marcus/Dana, directory search/filter, existing AI Experts segment, persisted note/custom field/tag, duplicate detection and merge, and final directory screenshot.
observations: Organizer shell has explicit top-level Speaker CRM navigation at /app/crm, distinct from per-event Speakers; current event switcher visible and demo identity Jordan Alvarez.

CRM import created 3 contacts with validation table; directory grew from 11 to 14. Search and company filter worked. Segment area already contained AI Experts (3 contacts) plus Confirmed speakers; custom dropdown Speaker Type Internal/External existed and External persisted; ad-hoc AI=yes also persisted. Priya profile note persisted and activity feed showed it. Event history section exists but showed no linked events for imported contact.

Duplicate test: manually created Priya Raman with alternate email; profile immediately showed Possible duplicates by same name. Clicking Merge into this merged original Priya record into the alternate-email record; directory remained 14 because this was a new record plus one merge, and activity recorded 'Merged duplicate Priya Raman <priya.raman@sbek-test.example.com>'. No side-by-side comparison screen was offered.

The app is credential-free demo persona simulation rather than signup/password auth; organizer shell entered via Jordan Alvarez card. Current event switcher offered AI Engineer Summit and CRM profile event selector offered DevFlow Conf 2027, demonstrating cross-event association support.

scenarios.scenarioName: Source a speaker through the pipeline and reuse across events
scenarios.summary: Verified seeded cross-event CRM: pipeline board and stage transitions, Marcus enrollment, persisted note and timestamped history, DevFlow event linking result, bulk mock campaign and history. Captured screenshots for board, enrollment, detail, event result, composer, send state, and campaign history. Noted missing score/rationale fields, no resolved personalization preview, weak event-history/roster visibility, and no dedicated CRM analytics dashboard.
observations: CRM is seeded and credential-free persona simulation; no signup/login form was required. DevFlow Conf 2027 already exists in the event switcher (Moscone West SF). Directory showed 14 contacts including Marcus Okafor, Priya Raman, and Dana Kowalski.

Sourcing pipeline exists at /app/crm/pipeline with stage columns Prospect, Contacted, Invited, Confirmed, Alumni, Declined. Marcus was enrolled and moved Prospect→Contacted→Invited; stage timeline is timestamped. Pipeline supports stage buttons rather than drag/drop and has no score/rationale fields in the enroll flow.

Marcus detail persisted internal note 'Left voicemail 2027-01-15; follow up next week.' and stage timeline. Add-to-event action offered DevFlow Conf 2027 and returned 'Already linked to event' / confirmed state; directory event count became 1, but CRM detail's Event history remained 'No linked events yet' and no separate event speaker roster for Marcus was surfaced.

Bulk Communicate exists: selected Marcus and Dana, composed subject 'Speak at DevFlow Conf 2027?' and body with {{name}}. Sent via mock mailer; campaign history shows 1 campaign, 2 recipients, and per-recipient recent activity entries (mock_sent). Composer exposed raw merge tag and no resolved personalization preview.

No separate CRM dashboard/overview with org-wide KPI analytics widgets was found. CRM directory has Contacts 14 KPI, Segments 2, Campaigns count, stage counts, top tag, and recent activity. Contacts KPI 14 matches the 14 visible directory contacts. /app/crm/overview fell back to landing page.

areas.title: Speaker Management

items.reasoning: A dedicated Speakers area lists each speaker with name plus title · company (Priya Raman · Principal Engineer · Latticework Systems; Marcus Okafor · Staff Developer Advocate · Cloudreach Labs). Typing 'Priya' in the search box narrowed the roster to only Priya's card, and after clearing the search the full roster (Dana, Marcus, Priya) rendered again.
evidence_refs: obs: Search narrowed to Priya and clear restored roster

items.reasoning: The Add speaker modal accepts name, email, title, company, bio (and travel preference), and the saved records display name/title/company on the roster and email/title/company/bio on the detail record. The organizer bio edit sentinel SBEK-ORG-EDIT-01 is shown saved on Priya's record, and the agent recorded that it persisted after reload (the reloaded record screenshot shows the same profile with the bio field below the fold).
evidence_refs: obs: Priya bio sentinel SBEK-ORG-EDIT-01 persisted after reload

items.reasoning: An 'Import CSV' control opens an import modal (with a column note and dedupe-by-email behaviour); the speakers.csv fixture was uploaded and afterward the roster/progress table contains a new Dana Kowalski record (Engineering Manager · Substrate) alongside the two manually added speakers, with the Priya/Marcus rows deduped rather than duplicated.
evidence_refs: screenshots/008-search-priya.jpg (image 5, progress table now lists Dana Kowalski)
obs: CSV import was available and imported Dana Kowalski plus CSV variants were deduped by email

items.reasoning: Priya's record has a Workflow status select with an Update status action that reported 'Workflow status updated to Confirmed.'; the confirmed badge then appears on the roster/progress table and is still confirmed in a later, separate session (SPK-S3), proving persistence. A 'Filter by workflow status' control exists and correctly returned an empty result set when set to confirmed at a time when all three speakers were still 'invited'. Gap in evidence: the status filter was not re-exercised after Priya became confirmed, so only negative (correct-empty) narrowing was captured.
evidence_refs: SPK-S3/screenshots/013-speaker-progress-list.jpg (image 32, Priya still confirmed in later session)
obs: Priya status changed to confirmed and persisted on reload

items.reasoning: The Assign task modal offers templates, title, description, due date, a Type selector (Action / confirm) and a multi-select assignee list; two speakers (Marcus + Priya) were selected and the modal reported '2 task(s) assigned · Marcus Okafor, Priya Raman'. The three fixture general tasks then appear organizer-side with due dates on Priya's record (Confirm participation due 2027-04-01, Complete bio and profile due 2027-04-01) and as per-speaker columns in the list-level progress table (Complete bio and profile / Confirm participation / Sign speaker release form) showing Marcus and Priya as assignees and Dana as unassigned ('—').
evidence_refs: obs: Created three GENERAL/action tasks via templates, assigned to both Marcus and Priya ... due dates

items.reasoning: Explicit invite controls exist both per-speaker on the roster cards ('Send invite') and on the speaker detail record ('Send portal invite'); the agent triggered it and recorded a successful send, and the app has a per-recipient send log in Comms where sends are recorded. No screenshot of the invite-specific success toast was captured, so the success state rests on the agent's observation (delivery itself is not agent-verifiable).
evidence_refs: obs: Portal invite control exists and was triggered successfully

items.reasoning: The /p portal is a distinct speaker-facing shell ('Ruckus Speaker portal', persona 'Priya Raman · speaker') with Home/Talks/Tasks/Deliverables/Resources/Profile, showing only Priya's tasks, her submissions/session, and her own profile. No Marcus or Dana data appears anywhere in the captured portal views, and when the speaker persona tried to open an organizer URL the app blocked it with 'Organizer access required'.
evidence_refs: turn 23 (SPK-S3): 'Organizer access required — You are signed in as Priya Raman (speaker)'
obs: No Marcus Okafor or Dana Kowalski data is visible on this dashboard

items.reasoning: Portal profile editing saved title, company, LinkedIn, X/Twitter and the sentinel bio 'SBEK-PORTAL-BIO-01 …', and after navigating back/reloading /p/profile the sentinel bio plus a rendered headshot avatar (alt 'Priya Raman headshot') are present. The agent then verified organizer-side sync, reporting that Priya's organizer record shows the portal bio sentinel and the headshot image plus headshot.png in Files/Deliverables. The organizer-side bio/headshot are asserted by observation rather than shown in the attached crop (bio and files sections sit below the fold), which is why confidence is medium.
evidence_refs: obs (SPK-S3): Organizer roster synced Priya's portal bio sentinel SBEK-PORTAL-BIO-01 and headshot; organizer record shows image

items.reasoning: The portal task list does show tasks with due dates and completion state that persists: two tasks flipped from To do/Pending to 'Done' and remained Done after reload while two others stayed Pending. However, the three organizer-created general tasks (Confirm participation, Complete bio and profile, Sign speaker release form) never appeared in Priya's portal — the portal listed only the four seeded event tasks (profile, headshot, slides, supporting document) because the portal was scoped to a different event (AI Engineer Summit) than the organizer workspace (DevFlow Conf 2027), even though the portal completions synced back into the DevFlow record. So the assigned-general-task visibility half is unmet.
evidence_refs: SPK-S2/screenshots/005-auto-p-tasks.jpg (image 15, all pending with due dates)
obs: Required script tasks Confirm participation and Sign speaker release form are absent
obs: Seeded event is AI Engineer Summit rather than sample DevFlow Conf 2027
SPK-S3/screenshots/010-auto-app-speakers-spk-ec5545ac.jpg (image 29, DevFlow record shows the 3 general tasks still 'To do')

items.reasoning: The uploaded file is tracked with filename and UTC timestamps and versions in the portal ('headshot.png · uploaded 2026-08-12 02:51:28 UTC', v1/v2 with View links), and the agent recorded that Priya's organizer record lists headshot.png with timestamps plus View/download links; clicking the download control opened the file API URL (…/content/files/content-f0f4ca11/versions/version-b7a02650) in a new tab without an error. The organizer-side listing itself is evidenced by observation/transcript rather than an attached crop.
evidence_refs: obs (SPK-S3): organizer record shows ... headshot.png files with timestamps plus View/download links. Download control opened a new tab successfully

items.reasoning: Priya's organizer record shows a SESSIONS panel containing 'Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale' with a 'Link speaker to an existing session' selector, and the same session appears in her portal Talks page as 'Organizer-linked session · 9:00 AM–9:45 AM Los Angeles · Main Hall' with a Scheduled badge.

The Speakers list page carries an ONBOARDING PROGRESS matrix (speaker × task) visible without opening records: Priya shows 33% with 'done' badges on the tasks she completed in the portal and 'open' on the rest, Marcus shows 0% with every task open, and Dana shows '—' for tasks she isn't assigned. This is a genuine list-level view that reflects portal completions (compare the all-0%/open table before the portal session). Readiness filters (Ready / Not ready) narrow membership consistently (Ready → no matches at 0/3 ready; Not ready → the unready speakers). The specific tasks marked done are 'Complete your speaker profile' and 'Upload headshot' rather than the fixture pair, a consequence of the portal event-scoping mismatch (see SPK-09), not of this view.

The Comms compose flow offers recipient selection over the speaker list (All speakers (3) plus per-speaker checkboxes), accepted the exact fixture subject 'Welcome to DevFlow Conf 2027 speakers' with a body, and 'Send to selected (3)' produced a success state ('Sent to 3 recipients · 4:53:50 AM'). A PER-RECIPIENT SEND LOG records each message with recipient name/email, ISO timestamp and rendered body, with explicit mock-delivery labelling.
evidence_refs: obs: bulk send succeeded to 3 recipients (mock). Send log shows each recipient and timestamp

items.reasoning: A TEMPLATES list (CFP received, Acceptance, Rejection, Task reminder, Schedule locked) is offered in the compose flow and template bodies contain merge tokens ({{first_name}}, {{talk_title}}, {{portal_link}}), with the supported merge field list displayed. Tokens demonstrably resolve per recipient: the send log renders 'Hi Priya, welcome to DevFlow Conf 2027!' and 'Hi Marcus, welcome to DevFlow Conf 2027!', and the agent recorded the Preview merge resolving {{first_name}} to Dana.
evidence_refs: obs: Comms supports merge fields and per-recipient preview ... preview resolved {{first_name}} to Dana

items.reasoning: The speaker record has a LOGISTICS section with 'Travel preference' (plus 'Dietary requirements'), and the add-speaker form also exposes Travel preference. The value entered from the portal ('Arrival May 11, aisle seat; dietary: Vegetarian') is shown as a saved value on the organizer record across subsequent navigations/reloads.
evidence_refs: screenshots/005-priya-filled-form.jpg (image 2, Travel preference field on create form)
obs: Priya's portal upload also persisted travel preference 'Arrival May 11, aisle seat; dietary: Vegetarian' after returning to organizer record

defects.description: Event scoping between the organizer workspace and the speaker portal is inconsistent: with the organizer workspace on DevFlow Conf 2027, Priya's portal opened on 'AI Engineer Summit' and listed only that event's four seeded tasks, so the three general tasks the organizer had just assigned to her (Confirm participation, Complete bio and profile, Sign speaker release form) were invisible in the portal — yet her portal profile/headshot completions did write back into the DevFlow Conf 2027 record. Speakers therefore cannot see (or complete) tasks the organizer assigned in the active event without discovering the portal's separate event switcher.
A single headshot submission produced two file versions (v1 and v2, timestamps 1.5s apart) on the deliverable, suggesting a double-submit on upload.
defects.where: Speaker portal task page /p/tasks/task-sub-...-headshot ('Uploaded file · 2 versions')

defects.description: The task-scoped 'Complete your speaker profile' form omits the headshot chooser that exists on the main /p/profile page, so a speaker following the task link cannot supply the headshot from that form.

Task rows label descriptions/types inconsistently (e.g. 'Confirm details' as the description of 'Confirm participation', 'Complete speaker profile' reused for two distinct tasks), making the organizer task list ambiguous.
defects.where: Organizer speaker record TASKS panel / onboarding progress columns

areas.notes: All three scenarios completed, giving broad coverage. The clone (Ruckus) implements the roster, add/import, workflow status, general tasks with multi-assignee, list-level onboarding matrix, a speaker portal with scoped content, templated bulk comms with merge fields and a per-recipient send log, plus travel/dietary logistics fields. The main functional weakness is the portal's event scoping (see defects), which prevented the three organizer-assigned general tasks from surfacing in Priya's portal and forced SPK-09 to partial; SPK-12 still passes because the list-level matrix demonstrably reflects the portal completions that did occur. Items marked auto-partial (SPK-06, SPK-07, SPK-10, SPK-13) were judged only on their UI-observable half; for SPK-08 and SPK-10 the organizer-side confirmation rests partly on the agent's recorded observations because the relevant panels sat below the screenshot fold. The status filter was exercised before Priya's status change, so only a correct-empty result was captured for the confirmed filter.

scenarios.scenarioName: Organizer builds the speaker roster and assigns onboarding tasks
scenarios.summary: Built DevFlow Conf 2027 speaker roster with Priya and Marcus, CSV import, search/filter, confirmed status persistence, bio edit persistence, linked/renamed Priya session, three shared general tasks with due dates, and verified portal invite control.
observations: Organizer shell is credential-free persona simulation. DevFlow Conf 2027 was pre-seeded and selected via event switcher; no creation was needed. Speakers roster supports manual add, CSV import, search, workflow status, record editing, sessions, general tasks, and portal invites.

Added Priya Raman and Marcus Okafor manually with title/company/bio; CSV import was available and imported Dana Kowalski plus CSV variants were deduped by email. Search narrowed to Priya and clear restored roster. Priya status changed to confirmed and persisted on reload.

Priya bio sentinel SBEK-ORG-EDIT-01 persisted after reload. Session title was renamed to 'Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale' and remains linked on Priya record. Portal invite control exists and was triggered successfully (invite logging indicated on initial add; explicit send control present).

Created three GENERAL/action tasks via templates, assigned to both Marcus and Priya: Confirm participation due 2027-04-01; Complete bio and profile due 2027-04-01; Sign speaker release form due 2027-04-15. Priya record after reload shows all three tasks and due dates. App's task list labels descriptions/type inconsistently but uses general-task modal, not file requests.
